text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israelis and Palestinians agree on pending issues.

- At its meeting under Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri on Sunday, the ministerial committee on privatisation will discuss a timetable for selling 12 profitable public-sector companies. The programme is to sell tranches of 20 percent, 51 percent or 90 percent of the shares for a total value of 1.4 billion pounds ($410 million). The sale will start this month and continue until the end of March. It includes selling off 30 percent of Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN through a GDR in early March and leasing 15 branches of internal trading companies to the private sector.
- President Hosni Mubarak received a phone call from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on the future of the peace process. Netanyahu also gave Mubarak Eid greetings.

- The head of the General Organisation for Investment, Ibrahim Fawzi, said that the investment value of projects received in December 1996 and January 1997 was 7.478 billion pounds, compared with 1.501 billion in the same period a year earlier, in other words an increase of 298 percent.
- EgyptAir has received permission from the U.N. sanctions committee to fly Libyan pilgrims to Saudi Arabia for the pilgrimage, as in the past two years.

- A report on the performance of the Egyptian economy indicates that investment activity has had positive results, that inflation has fallen by 20 percent to less than seven percent and that the Egyptian pound has strengthened against other currencies. The report was prepared by the Information and Decision Support Centre of the cabinet office.
- The Capital Market Authority has agreed that 68 companies can raise their capital by about 860 million pounds by issuing 14.5 million shares.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will soon discuss a new law drafted by the industry ministry which requires producers of electrical goods and household appliances to have service centres in Egypt.
- Banks, private-sector companies and public-sector companies resume work today after Eid al-Fitr.
- The mobile telephone service will reach Alexandria during March. The north coast, the Cairo-Alexandria road, Luxor and Aswan will follow.
